# firecrawl crawl

Bulk extract content from a website. Crawls pages following links up to a depth/limit.

**Prerequisite:** `crawl` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

## Quick start

```bash
# Crawl a docs section
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --include-paths /docs --limit 50 --wait -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Full crawl with depth limit
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --max-depth 3 --wait --progress -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Check status of a running crawl
firecrawl crawl <job-id>
```

Run `firecrawl crawl --help` for the full option list.

**Done when:** the crawl reaches a terminal status and the saved output under `.firecrawl/` contains the expected pages.

## Tips

- Use `--wait` when you need the results immediately. It has no default timeout; use `--timeout <seconds>` to bound polling. Without `--wait`, crawl returns a job ID for async polling.
- **One crawl, not a scrape loop.** If you're about to scrape a third page from the same site or section, crawl it instead with `--limit`.
- **Scope crawls with `--include-paths`** whenever the request names a section — crawl only the pages you need.
- Crawl consumes credits per page. Check `firecrawl credit-usage` before large crawls (`credit-usage` requires authentication).

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape individual pages
- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — discover URLs before deciding to crawl
- [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md) — download site to local files (uses map + scrape)
- [firecrawl-build-scrape](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-scrape) — building bulk extraction into an app instead of running it here

I scraped all 340 method pages in Slack's Web API reference (docs.slack.dev/reference/methods) and read the rate-limit line on each one. I took tiers from each page's own "Rate Limits" line, not the index.

## Tier 1 (1+ per minute): 17 methods
- `admin.apps.uninstall`
- `admin.conversations.restrictAccess.removeGroup`
- `admin.teams.create`
- `admin.usergroups.addChannels`

- `apps.manifest.update`
- `apps.uninstall`
- `conversations.listConnectInvites`
- `rtm.connect`
- `rtm.start`
- `team.externalTeams.disconnect`

## "Special rate limits apply": 18 methods
- `admin.analytics.messages.metadata`
- `agents.conversations.archive`
- `agents.conversations.create`
- `agents.conversations.listViews`
- `agents.conversations.removeView`
- `agents.conversations.setCommands`
- `agents.conversations.setProperties`
- `agents.conversations.setView`
- `apps.event.authorizations.list`
- `assistant.search.context`
- `assistant.threads.setStatus`
- `auth.test`
- `blocks.validate`
- `chat.getPermalink`
- `chat.postMessage`
- `oauth.v2.access`
- `oauth.v2.user.access`
- `tooling.tokens.rotate`

## All `conversations.*` methods (28)

| Tier | Methods |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 (1+/min) | `listConnectInvites` |
| Tier 2 (20+/min) | `acceptSharedInvite`, `archive`, `canvases.create`, `close`, `create`, `externalInvitePermissions.set`, `inviteShared`, `list`, `rename`, `requestSharedInvite.approve`, `requestSharedInvite.deny`, `requestSharedInvite.list`, `setPurpose`, `setTopic`, `unarchive` |
| Tier 3 (50+/min) | `approveSharedInvite`, `declineSharedInvite`, `history`, `info`, `invite`, `join`, `kick`, `leave`, `mark`, `open`, `replies` |
| Tier 4 (100+/min) | `members` |

## Deprecated on their own page
Only one page carries a deprecation notice at the top: **`files.upload`**. It says the method "will stop functioning and be officially sunset on November 12, 2025". Slack's replacement is `files.getUploadURLExternal` plus `files.completeUploadExternal`.

Every page lists `method_deprecated` and `deprecated_endpoint` among its generic error codes. I ignored those, since they aren't a deprecation of the method itself.

## Things to check for your rate-limit problem
- **`conversations.history` and `conversations.replies`:** both are listed as Tier 3. Each page also says that since May 29, 2025, apps distributed commercially outside the Marketplace get only 1 request per minute. For those apps, the `limit` parameter is capped at 15, and the default is also 15. Marketplace apps and internal customer-built apps keep Tier 3. I confirmed this text on `conversations.history`. I didn't check `replies` for the same wording, so read that page too.
- **`chat.postMessage`:** it's "special", not tiered. I didn't pull the exact figure, so check the page.
- **`slacklists.access.set`:** its page has no rate-limit line at all, so it isn't in any tier above.
- **Index vs. page-name counts:** the index links 338 distinct methods, but a few appear under two spellings. I deduplicated these case-insensitively to get 340 pages. The raw pages and my tier table are in `/tmp/fceval-c1-t2-zoohvf34/work/out/`. My table has lowercase method names, so the capitalization above is restored by hand.
